faq.question: How do I install Rolodink?
faq.answer: Add Rolodink with one click from the Chrome Web Store, Edge Add-ons or Firefox Add-ons. It works on LinkedIn right after installation. Refresh the page if you don't see the sidebar right away.

faq.question: How do my notes get secured?
faq.answer: Your notes are stored encrypted and are only visible to you in Rolodink. We never sell your data. More details are in the Privacy Policy.

faq.question: Is Rolodink really free?
faq.answer: Yes, the core functionality of Rolodink is completely free. Premium features for power users may come later, but the basics will remain free.

faq.question: Where are my notes stored?
faq.answer: Your notes are stored encrypted in the cloud, linked to your account. Only you can see them in Rolodink. We never sell your data. More details are in the Privacy Policy.

faq.question: Does Rolodink also work on the mobile LinkedIn app?
faq.answer: Rolodink currently works as a browser extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox on desktop computers. A mobile version is on our roadmap.

faq.question: I don't see the Rolodink sidebar on LinkedIn. What now?
faq.answer: Try refreshing the LinkedIn page. If that doesn't work, check if the extension is enabled via the puzzle piece icon in your Chrome toolbar. Contact us if the problem persists.

faq.question: Can I export my data?
faq.answer: Yes. In the extension settings you can download a readable export (CSV for Excel, or JSON) with your connections decrypted, and an encrypted backup (JSON) exactly as it is stored. The readable export is decrypted in the extension itself, so we never see your notes in readable form. That file does contain your notes, email addresses and phone numbers unencrypted, so keep it somewhere safe.

ChangelogPage.title: Changelog
ChangelogPage.description: Stay up to date with the latest developments and updates.

sections.title: Password
items: The sign-in screen now has a 'Forgot password?' link. It opens rolodink.app, where you request a link to choose a new password.
Passwords that appear in a known data breach are refused when you create an account or change your password. Your password itself never leaves your computer.
A new password needs at least 8 characters everywhere; changing it in the extension used to accept 6. Signing in with an existing password keeps working.

sections.title: Repairs
items: The update notice in the popup shows its buttons again. Only its header used to be visible, so all you could do was close it.
Your connection list works from the keyboard: Tab to choose, Enter or Space to open.
Errors on Esc and Alt+L are now logged instead of disappearing unnoticed.

sections.title: New in the popup
items: Add, edit and search an email address and phone number. One click opens your mail or dials, "+31 (0)6 …" included. Both are stored encrypted.
Readable export as JSON or CSV, decrypted in the extension itself. The CSV opens straight in Excel.
Outside a profile you see your list right away, with a button to send feedback.

sections.title: Your notes
items: If you edit the same connection in two places at once, you get a notice and choose which version stays. The last save used to win silently.
On some profiles the note field appeared briefly and then vanished. It now stays in the profile header.
The same profile no longer lands in your Rldnk twice through another variant of its link.

sections.title: Account and Firefox
items: Changing your password checks your current one, and deleting your account removes your login too.
Firefox 140 or later is required. Firefox now asks consent for the data Rolodink sends to its server.

sections.title: Faster
items: The popup opens faster, and the extension is smaller and lighter in the background.

sections.title: Your notes
items: If the note field can't load your existing note (the server is busy, your session expired), it now stays closed and offers Retry. It used to open empty, and what you typed replaced your saved note.
A note still being saved when you moved on to the next profile could end up on that profile. It now stays with the profile you wrote it on.

sections.title: In the popup
items: Editing a connection no longer clears its email and phone.
A note that couldn't be decrypted is no longer overwritten when you save an edit.
Deleting a connection no longer leaves your notes unencrypted in your browser's storage.
Deleting your account works in English too: it asked for "DELETE" but only accepted "VERWIJDER".

sections.title: Permissions
items: Rolodink asks for fewer permissions: it no longer needs access to your browser tabs.

sections.title: For Firefox
items: The note field on profile pages now works in Firefox too. It never did: Firefox ran a separate part that had fallen behind.
"Add to Rldnk" sits in the large profile card next to Message, not in the narrow bar that only appears once you scroll.
Rolodink follows your clicks inside LinkedIn in Firefox as well, and the button and note field move with you to the next profile.
In short: Firefox is level with Chrome and Edge again.

sections.title: For everyone
items: Type a note on someone who is not in your Rolodink yet and they are now added for you. Your text used to be dropped with a message telling you to add them first.
The note field calls it "Rldnk" now, like the button beside it.

sections.title: For Chrome and Edge
items: Nothing beyond that: the Firefox part of this release does not touch your browser.

sections.title: Delivery fix
items: Nothing changes in the extension itself. A fault in our release process delayed v1.3.4 for Chrome and Edge; this version delivers it there.
Coming from v1.3.3 or older, this is what brings you the nine fixes for LinkedIn's August 2026 redesign — see v1.3.4 below.

sections.title: On LinkedIn
items: LinkedIn rebuilt its profile pages, which made "Add to Rldnk" and the note field disappear. Both are back.
They now sit in the large profile card next to Message, not in the narrow bar that only appears once you scroll.
The note field sits below that card instead of floating over the navigation bar.
Note: in this version the profile-page note field did not work in Firefox yet. Fixed in 1.3.6.
Rolodink now follows your clicks inside LinkedIn: a profile opened from your feed or a search result works too.
The button and note field move with you to the next profile, carrying the right details.

sections.title: Saving and signing in
items: Notes save again; every call from the LinkedIn page was being blocked.
Add a profile after opening the note field and your text is now kept.
Signing in from the onboarding page did not sign the extension in; that page now points at the popup.
Signing out clears the stored encryption key.

sections.title: Under the hood
items: This version never reached the stores, so you did not miss it. Its contents ship in v1.3.4.
No visible changes: this release only reorganises how Rolodink is built.
The code that runs on LinkedIn pages is now built from the same shared source as the popup, so a fix has one place to live instead of three.
Automated tests now run on every change before it can be released.

sections.title: Interface
items: Editing a connection now shows whose details you are changing.
"New Connection" appeared twice; now it appears once.
The update notice no longer pushes the rest of the popup out of view.
Signing up lands on the right page again instead of a 404.

sections.title: Important fix for notes
items: Notes edited in the note field on a LinkedIn profile are now stored encrypted correctly.
That field shows your note as readable text again, instead of encrypted code.
If a note cannot be decrypted, the field is locked rather than overwritten.
Notes from older versions stay readable and are encrypted on their next edit.

sections.title: Automatic Encryption
items: No more passphrase: your data is encrypted automatically once you're signed in.
Encryption uses a secure per-account key managed by the server.
Security fix: saving can no longer silently fall back to unencrypted data.
Key management is tied to your account; the key is cleared on logout.
Note: since this version the key is managed by the server, so encryption is no longer end-to-end. Notes are still encrypted before they are stored.

sections.title: End-to-End Encryption & Onboarding
items: End-to-end encryption extended to email, phone, meeting place and company.
Migration tool to encrypt existing data.
Redesigned onboarding with a step-by-step guide.
Email and phone fields added to connections.

sections.title: Critical Hotfix
items: Fixed issue with missing background credentials.
Ensured stable connection to backend.

sections.title: Refinements & Fixes
items: Updated contact information.
Stability improvements for backend connections.
General performance optimizations.

sections.title: Edge Support
items: Rolodink is now available in the Microsoft Edge Add-ons store.
Full note synchronization between Chrome and Edge.

sections.title: Improved Performance
items: Faster load times when opening profiles.
Optimized memory usage.

sections.title: Firefox Support
items: Full release for Mozilla Firefox.
All features now available for Firefox users.

sections.title: Bug Fixes
items: Minor improvements to the user interface.
Stability updates for reliable data storage.

sections.title: Cross-Browser Support
items: Full support for Firefox (Manifest V2).
Full support for Microsoft Edge.
Unified build system for Chrome, Firefox, and Edge.

sections.title: Background Authentication
items: Authentication moved to persistent background service worker.
Fixed: Authentication failed if popup was closed.
Improved session detection for seamless login.

sections.title: Bug Fixes
items: Fixed: Infinite reload loop in certain situations.
Improved build system stability.

sections.title: Chrome Web Store Release
items: Successful publication in the Chrome Web Store.
Optimized permissions (strictly necessary only).
Improved validation during the build process.

sections.title: Initial Release
items: First public version of Rolodink.
Add notes to LinkedIn profiles.
End-to-end encryption for notes.
Secure data storage with Supabase.

SecurityPage.title: Security
SecurityPage.intro: Notes about the people in your network are personal. This page explains how Rolodink protects them, and where the limits are.

sections.title: Encryption
paragraphs: Your notes, meeting place, company, email and phone number are encrypted with AES-256-GCM inside the browser extension before they are sent to us, and that is how they are stored. Entries saved with older versions of the extension, from before this encryption was added, can still be stored unencrypted; they are encrypted as soon as you edit and save them. Traffic between the extension and our servers runs over HTTPS.

Every account has its own encryption key. We generate it on first use and store it wrapped with a master key that is kept as a secret in our hosting environment, separate from the database. The extension keeps your key in memory and session storage only while you are signed in, and clears it when you sign out.

What this is not: end-to-end or zero-knowledge encryption. Because we manage the keys, your notes are available on every device you sign in on, but it also means that someone with access to both our database and our master key could decrypt them. We would rather say that plainly than overstate it.

sections.title: Access control
paragraphs: Row-Level Security is enabled on the database, so an account can only read its own rows, even if another layer were to fail. Sign-in runs through Supabase authentication with token-based sessions.

sections.title: Protection against abuse
paragraphs: The API applies rate limits per IP address, with a stricter limit for signing in and signing up. The API only accepts requests from approved origins (CORS allowlist), and user input is validated before it is processed.

sections.title: Secrets and dependencies
paragraphs: API keys and secrets are stored as environment variables and are never committed to the code. Every commit is automatically scanned for leaked secrets, and our dependencies are checked for known vulnerabilities as part of our build pipeline.

sections.title: Your data, your control
paragraphs: You can export all your data or delete your account and everything stored with it at any time. If deleting your account from the extension does not work for you, email privacy@rolodink.app and we will delete it for you. Your notes are private: the people you write about cannot see them, and we never sell your data or share it for anyone else's purposes. We use Supabase and Vercel to host Rolodink.

sections.title: Reporting a vulnerability
paragraphs: Found a security issue, or have a question about how we handle your data? Email us and we will respond as soon as we can.

FAQ.title: Frequently Asked Questions
FAQ.subtitle: Everything you need to know about Rolodink

why.question: Why Rolodink? Aren't there enough CRM systems?
why.answer: Rolodink is specifically designed for LinkedIn and focuses on personal notes instead of complex CRM functions.

free.question: Is Rolodink really free?
free.answer: Yes, Rolodink is completely free to use as a browser extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox. No credit card required, no limits.

security.question: How secure are my notes?
security.answer: Your notes are encrypted with AES-256 in your browser before they are stored, and only you can see them in Rolodink. Every account has its own key. We manage those keys so your notes work on every device, which means this is not end-to-end encryption in the strict sense. Read the details on our security page.

mobile.question: Does Rolodink work on mobile?
mobile.answer: Not yet. Rolodink is a browser extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox on desktop. A mobile version is on our roadmap.

export.question: Can I export my notes?
export.answer: Yes. In the extension settings you can download a readable export (CSV for Excel, or JSON) with your connections decrypted, and an encrypted backup (JSON) exactly as it is stored. The readable export is decrypted in the extension itself, so we never see your notes in readable form. That file does contain your notes, email addresses and phone numbers unencrypted, so keep it somewhere safe.

visibility.question: Do others see my notes on LinkedIn?
visibility.answer: No. Your notes are only visible in Rolodink, and only to you.

browser.question: Does this work in my browser?
browser.answer: Rolodink works in all Chromium-based browsers, including Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave, and Opera. A Firefox version is also available.

legal.question: Does Rolodink comply with privacy laws?
legal.answer: Rolodink is built on GDPR principles: we collect only what the service needs, you can export or delete your data at any time, and we never sell it or share it for anyone else's purposes. We use hosting and database providers (Supabase and Vercel) to run the service.

support.question: What about updates and support?
support.answer: Rolodink is regularly updated with new features and security patches. Support is available via our Help Center.

benefits.title: Quick add
benefits.description: One click from the profile, and the note is saved as you type.

limits: Rolodink is a desktop browser extension. A mobile version is on the roadmap; until then, add your notes when you are back at your computer.
Follow-up reminders are on the roadmap. They are not available yet.
events.privacy: Your notes are encrypted with AES-256 in your browser before they are stored, and only you can see them in Rolodink. The people you met cannot see what you wrote.

faq.question: How do I add someone I just met?
faq.answer: Open their LinkedIn profile in your browser, click Add to Rldnk next to Message and write your note.

faq.question: Can I use Rolodink on my phone at the event?
faq.answer: Not yet. Rolodink is a desktop browser extension and a mobile version is on the roadmap. Add your notes when you are back at your computer.

faq.question: Will the person see what I wrote?
faq.answer: No. Your notes are only visible to you in Rolodink, not on LinkedIn and not to the person you write about.

howItWorks.title: How It Works: Add Notes to LinkedIn in 4 Steps
howItWorks.description: Install the free extension, open a profile, write a note and find the person again by name, company or any detail. That is how Rolodink works.

download.title: Download Rolodink for Chrome, Edge & Firefox
download.description: Install the free Rolodink extension for LinkedIn from the Chrome Web Store, Edge Add-ons or Firefox Add-ons. Ready in 30 seconds, no credit card needed.

help.description: Answers about Rolodink: privacy, security, exporting notes, supported browsers and support. Can't find your question? Get in touch and we will help you out.

linkedinNotes.title: LinkedIn Notes Extension: Add Private Notes
linkedinNotes.description: Rolodink is a free browser extension for private notes on LinkedIn profiles. Write where you met and what you discussed, then find people by any detail.

useCaseRecruiters.title: Candidate Notes on LinkedIn for Recruiters
useCaseRecruiters.description: Keep a private note on every candidate's LinkedIn profile: when you spoke, what they want next and a personal detail. Free for Chrome, Edge and Firefox.

useCaseSales.title: LinkedIn Notes for Sales: Remember Every Prospect
useCaseSales.description: Keep a private note on each prospect's LinkedIn profile: what you sent, when an answer is due and a personal detail for a follow-up that sounds human. Free.

useCaseEvents.title: Remember People You Meet at Networking Events
useCaseEvents.description: Add a note to someone's LinkedIn profile while it is fresh: where you met, what you discussed and what you promised. Free for Chrome, Edge and Firefox.

OnboardingPage.title: Welcome to Rolodink
OnboardingPage.intro: Three steps and you're ready for your first note.

pin.title: Pin the extension
pin.description: Click the puzzle piece icon in your toolbar and pin Rolodink for easy access.

login.title: Sign in from the extension
login.description: Signing in happens inside the Rolodink window itself. You can create your account there too.

instructions.open: Click the Rolodink icon in your toolbar to open the window.
instructions.choose: Pick "Sign Up" for a new account or "Log In" if you already have one. Both work with LinkedIn or with email.
instructions.note: Signing in on this website does not sign in the extension: they are two separate sessions. Only signing in from the extension window counts.

vault.title: Automatic encryption
vault.description: Rolodink encrypts your private details automatically once you're signed in. You do not need a separate passphrase.
